documents.title: Form for School
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Our school nurse needs a form signed by my doctor so I can keep my auto-injectors in the classroom and so she has an emergency plan on file for me. I attached the blank one. Thank you!

documents.title: Medication Authorization for School
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the school nurse:
Lisa O'Brien (DOB 03/15/1990) has a latex allergy with a history of anaphylaxis. She is authorized to carry and self-administer epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injectors at work. In an emergency: inject into the outer thigh, call 911, and a second dose may be given after 5 to 15 minutes if symptoms persist. Please keep latex balloons and latex gloves out of her classroom and the nurse's office supplies she may use.
Form completed and signed; returned to patient through the portal.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Interval: big year. Anaphylaxis in January during the nevus excision; allergy found latex IgE positive in March. Nevus benign. No reactions since. Carries two auto-injectors, school has her plan. One small cold sore over the summer, treated at home. Eczema quiet through the warm months. Allergies better this spring with daily spray.

Meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN; cetirizine 10 mg PRN; fluticasone nasal daily; valacyclovir 1 g episodic; epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector.
Allergies: LATEX (anaphylaxis); dust mite, tree pollen (rhinitis).
Social: started the new school year last month. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

ROS: negative.
Exam: Vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal; lips clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. Skin: well-healed linear scar left upper back; no eczema active today. No edema.

A/P:
- Preventive: PHQ-9 1. CBC, CMP, lipids today. Flu and COVID given, latex-free supplies confirmed before the injections. Pap/HPV co-test due next year.
- Latex allergy with history of anaphylaxis: avoidance, auto-injectors current; renewal due in January.
- Atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, herpes labialis: stable, no changes.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Physical Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisa, all of last week's bloodwork is normal. Have a good fall.

documents.title: Eye Problem
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I ended up in the ER yesterday with my right eye. It had been red and painful for three days and getting blurry, and the light was killing me. The eye doctor there said it was herpes on the cornea, the same virus as my cold sores, and gave me an antiviral eye gel to use 5 times a day. I have a follow-up with them next week. I am out of school for a few days. Just wanted you to know.

documents.title: RE: Eye Problem
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know, and I'm sorry, that is a painful one. Use the gel exactly as they told you and keep the follow-up with ophthalmology; they will guide how long to continue it. Don't touch the eye and then your lips or the other eye, and wash hands after the gel. If vision gets worse or the pain spikes before your appointment, go back to them. Please book a visit with me after you've seen them.

medications.sig: 1 drop in the right eye 5 times daily until the ulcer heals, then 3 times daily for 7 days

documents.title: Emergency Department Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, OPHTHALMOLOGY CONSULT
Date of service: 10/14/2025
Patient: Lisa O'Brien, 35 F

CC: right eye pain, redness, blurred vision x 3 days.
HPI: 35-year-old woman with recurrent HSV-1 cold sores (orolabial outbreak with buccal lesions October 2024) and anaphylaxis during a skin procedure in January 2025, attributed to latex. Three days ago it felt like something was in the right eye; then tearing, light sensitivity, worsening pain and blur. No trauma. No contact lens use. Left eye fine.
PMH: atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, recurrent herpes labialis, anaphylaxis history.
Meds: mometasone ointment PRN, cetirizine PRN, fluticasone nasal, valacyclovir episodic, epinephrine auto-injector.
Allergies: LATEX (anaphylaxis); dust mite, tree pollen.

Exam:
Visual acuity (sc): OD 20/60, OS 20/20.
Pupils equal and reactive, no APD.
OD: conjunctival injection. Cornea with several small epithelial vesicles and a branching dendritic ulcer that takes up fluorescein. No purulent discharge. Anterior chamber deep and quiet.
OS: normal anterior segment.
IOP normal both eyes.

Impression: herpes simplex epithelial keratitis, right eye.
Plan: ganciclovir 0.15% ophthalmic gel, 1 drop OD 5 times daily until the epithelium heals, then 3 times daily for 7 days. No topical steroid. Ophthalmology clinic follow-up in about 10 days. Return sooner for worsening vision or pain.
Latex precautions observed during the exam.

events.reason: follow-up after ED visit for eye

conditions.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
conditions.note: right eye, dendritic epithelial ulcer, treated by ophthalmology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here after her 10/14 ER visit for the right eye. ER ophthalmology note received 10/30: dendritic ulcer right cornea, acuity 20/60 on that side, started on ganciclovir gel. She saw ophthalmology clinic on 10/24 and was told the ulcer had healed and her vision was back; she finished the 3-times-a-day taper last week. We do not yet have the clinic note. The eye feels normal now, no pain, no redness, reading fine. No new lip lesions.
O: Vitals as charted. Right eye white and quiet, no discharge, pupils equal. Reads the wall chart comfortably at near. Lips clear.
A: Herpes simplex keratitis, right eye, treated and healed per ophthalmology. Recurrent HSV-1 labialis.
P: Added to the problem list. Requested the ophthalmology clinic note. Any recurrence of eye pain, redness or blur goes straight to ophthalmology, not to waiting on us. Continue episodic valacyclovir for lip outbreaks. She will keep her ophthalmology follow-up schedule.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY CLINIC
Date of visit: 10/24/2025
Re: Lisa O'Brien, DOB 03/15/1990

Seen in follow-up for right herpes simplex epithelial keratitis diagnosed in the emergency department 10/14/2025, on ganciclovir 0.15% gel 5 times daily.
Today: pain and photophobia resolved.
Visual acuity: OD 20/20, OS 20/20.
Slit lamp OD: corneal epithelium healed, no residual staining with fluorescein; no stromal haze or infiltrate; anterior chamber quiet.
OS: normal.
Assessment: HSV epithelial keratitis OD, resolved.
Plan: reduce ganciclovir to 3 times daily for 7 days, then stop. Return promptly for any recurrence of redness, pain or blurred vision in either eye.
Allergies: latex (anaphylaxis); dust mite; tree pollen.

(Received by fax 01/08/2026 after a second request.)

medications.sig: Inject 0.3 mg into the outer thigh once for anaphylaxis; may repeat once after 5 to 15 minutes; call 911

documents.title: Prior Authorization and Renewal
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting a new prescription for epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injectors; her two-pack from January 2025 expires this month. Insurance prefers the generic; brand would need a PA. PCP sent generic, 2 two-packs (one for home, one for school), 1 refill. Patient notified by portal; she will drop the old pens off at the pharmacy.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Eczema up for three weeks with the cold snap: backs of the hands, wrists and elbow creases, itchy at night. Using mometasone on and off, plus hand cream, but she slipped on the night gloves. Has been extra careful about not using latex gloves for classroom cleanup. Eye has stayed fine since the fall. No cold sores this winter.
O: Vitals as charted. Dorsal hands and wrists with erythematous, scaly, slightly lichenified patches; a couple of shallow fissures. Antecubital fossae with mild erythema. No vesicles, crusts or pustules. Eyes white and quiet.
A: Atopic dermatitis, winter flare. Herpes simplex keratitis resolved; ophthalmology clinic letter arrived in January confirming healed cornea and 20/20.
P: Mometasone twice daily for 2 weeks, then twice weekly maintenance on the usual spots through March. Back to the ointment-and-cotton-glove routine at night. Vinyl or nitrile gloves only. Message in 3 weeks if not clearly better. Physical this summer with Pap.

documents.title: Spring Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Pollen season is here again. Could I get refills on the fluticasone and cetirizine? Hands cleared up nicely after the February visit.

documents.title: RE: Spring Refills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Both sent to your pharmacy per the doctor, with refills for the year. Your physical is booked for July 30 at 7:30 AM.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Interval: quiet year after a rough 2025. No allergic reactions; auto-injectors renewed in January and never needed. No eye trouble since the keratitis healed in October. Two small cold sores, both caught early with valacyclovir. Eczema flare in February settled. Spring allergies manageable with daily spray and cetirizine.

Meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN; cetirizine 10 mg PRN; fluticasone nasal daily; valacyclovir 1 g episodic; epinephrine 0.3 mg auto-injector.
Allergies: LATEX (anaphylaxis); dust mite, tree pollen (rhinitis).
Social: summer off, teaching again in late August. Never smoker; alcohol rare.

ROS negative.
Exam: Vitals as charted. Well. HEENT normal, eyes white, lips clear. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vagina and cervix normal; Pap/HPV collected with a nonlatex speculum and gloves. Skin: hands clear, old scar left upper back. No edema.

A/P:
- Preventive: PHQ-2 0. Pap with HPV co-test today (last 2021). CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu and COVID this fall; she will come by once vaccines arrive.
- Latex allergy with anaphylaxis history: avoidance, auto-injectors current.
- Atopic dermatitis: controlled; keep the winter routine.
- Allergic rhinitis: stable.
- Recurrent HSV-1 labialis: episodic valacyclovir, refills sent. History of HSV keratitis right eye, healed; she knows to go straight to ophthalmology for eye symptoms.
Follow-up in the fall for skin and allergies, then physical next summer.

documents.title: Physical Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, your Pap and HPV test are both normal, so the next one is in five years. Blood counts, chemistry and cholesterol from the 30th are all normal too. Enjoy the rest of the summer.

documents.title: RE: Physical Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great news, thank you! See you in November.
